item.title: Discord Rolling Out Age Verification Worldwide By March, Angering Users Across Social Media
item.description: The Discord Age Verification Controversy refers to reports that, by March 2026, the chat application Discord will require age verification worldwide via face scan or ID to access adult content, including age-restricted communities and blurred or marked-sensitive content shared in a Discord server. item.title: VTuber Inugami Korone's Catchphrase 'Water In The Fire Why?' Continues Generating Memes Online
item.description: Water In The Fire Why? refers to an Engrish catchphrase said by Hololive virtual YouTuber talent Inugami Korone in a clip while she's playing Super Mario Bros., in which she wonders how the fire bar obstacle is still burning while it's underwater. Her reaction became the subject of animations and other memes among the community in the 2020s.

item.title: Mysterious TikToker 'Dany Slicer' Becomes 2026's Ultimate Villain After Aura-Filled Photo Dump
item.description: Dany Slicer, often misspelled Danny Slicer, is a TikToker known for a series of video edit memes where images of him are edited to portray him as a stereotypical villain. item.title: CIA Whistleblower John Kiriakou's Insane Stories Inspire Brainrot Edits On TikTok
item.description: John Kiriakou CIA Story Edits refers to video clips and edits of CIA whistleblower John Kiriakou telling unbelievable stories about his time in the CIA as an intelligence officer. The edits, which often feature funny overlayed captions and slow motion effects, started going viral on TikTok in early February 2026 and were popularized by TikToker @_bamboclat.

item.title: Anime Series 'Kakegurui' Inspires Another Meme Trend Closely Related To The 'Yumeko Grab' Meme

item.title: Why This Song From 1944 Keeps Going Viral
item.description: Gays in 1944 or The Trolley Song refers to a viral TikTok trend in which “The Trolley Song, ” performed by Judy Garland for the 1944 film Meet Me in St. Louis, is utilized for memes, dance videos and remixes. The trend uses modern-day gay culture to jokingly exaggerate interpretations of the past, stemming from Garland’s longstanding veneration within the gay community.
